article.title: Everyday phone call phrases
article.description: Answering: 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' Asking to hold: 'Could you hold on a second?' Ending: 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!' Common mistake: 'I am [name]' on the phone sounds unnatural in English — 'This is [name]' is the standard phone convention.
article.content: Answering: 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' Asking to hold: 'Could you hold on a second?' Ending: 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!' Common mistake: 'I am [name]' on the phone sounds unnatural in English — 'This is [name]' is the standard phone convention.

generated.caption:
Ever said "I am [your name]" on the phone? 🤔 It's a common mistake!

The natural way is 'Hello, this is [name] speaking.' (e.g., 'Hello, this is Sarah speaking.') Need to ask someone to hold? 'Could you hold on a second?' To end: 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!' Simple!

slides.headlineRest: — The Right Way to Answer a Call
slides.body: When answering the phone in English, the standard and natural way to introduce yourself is 'Hello, this is [your name] speaking.' It might feel tempting to say 'I am [your name]', but this actually sounds unnatural and is considered a common mistake in English phone conversations. For example, if your name is Priya, you'd say, 'Hello, this is Priya speaking.' If you need someone to wait, simply ask, 'Could you hold on a second?' And to end the call politely, 'Thanks for calling, talk soon!'
slides.hindiSummary: फोन पर अपना परिचय देने का सही तरीका 'Hello, this is [आपका नाम] speaking' है, न कि 'I am [आपका नाम]'.
